claim_ceiling.rationale: with about 21 test clips the clip is the experimental unit and frames are correlated sub-samples; a frame or clip bootstrap is refused and the claim verb is bounded to 'consistent with', never 'demonstrates' or 'significant'

claim_scope: deterministic programmatic mechanics only; no capability or natural-data claim
direction: candidate < rate_matched_random (the trained gate places the same re-estimation budget better, reaching a lower count-MAE at matched re-estimation count)
metric: coasted concurrent-source count MAE (lower is better), pooled frame micro-average
metric_rule: coasted-count-MAE: emitted holds the last re-estimate, cold-start 0, pooled frame micro-average
operating_point_rule: the swept re-estimation budget whose fraction is closest to the train-set count-change density; a fixed rule set before scoring, using only train labels, never a val or test MAE argmax
promotion_bar: promote only when the registered SESOI is exceeded AND the one-sided sign-flip p clears alpha AND at least three bias-independent reproductions triangulate the same direction; a single run can never promote
question: concurrent-source COUNTING value-of-computation: does a trained gate reach lower coasted count-MAE at the same re-estimation budget as a rate-matched-random gate

sesoi.rationale: Cost-benefit SESOI on coasted count-MAE. The candidate and the rate-matched-random control spend the same re-estimation count K at equal FLOPs, so the amortized training cost C_train (8274960000 FLOPs, equal to 103437 re-estimation equivalents at C_reest = 80000 FLOPs) buys nothing but the count-MAE advantage of learned re-estimation placement over free random placement. At the operating re-estimation fraction 0.050 the per-re-estimation saving against always-on is 76000 FLOPs, so the gate does not even repay C_train until N* = 108,881 frames (about 3.0 hours of audio). Given that deployment scale, the smallest count-MAE win worth registering is one that is both measurable above the pseudoreplication floor and economically meaningful. Pooled MAE has a per-frame granularity of 4.43e-05 (1 / 22569 test frames), so the chosen SESOI of 0.02 is 451x the granularity floor (about 451 frame-errors), far above measurement noise. It also sits at about one test clip's worth of correctly tracked changes: the test fold carries 916 changes over 21 clips (43.6 per clip) with a mean run of 24.6 frames, so one clip's catchable change mass is about 537 frame-errors (0.0238 pooled MAE). A win below the SESOI recovers less than about one clip of change-tracking over free random placement and does not justify carrying a trained module over the zero-training control, so it is not promotable even if the one-sided sign-flip p clears alpha.
sesoi.selection_method: cost-benefit (deployment break-even plus one-test-clip change mass)

sign_flip_test_plan.statistic: mean of paired per-seed count-MAE deltas (rate_matched_random minus candidate)
sign_flip_test_plan.test: exact sign-flip permutation, one-sided, upper tail
